---
title: "Directionality Assessment: AGES vs AddNeuroMed Study"
---

## Overview

This analysis assesses whether DNA methylation effect directions are consistent between AGES and the AddNeuroMed cohort using binomial sign tests to evaluate concordance significance.

The input, `es_long_filtered_AddNeuroMed.rds`, is already trimmed once by `05_AddNeuroMed_comparison.qmd` (central 95% of each axis, per comparison), the same data behind the Figure 5B correlations, and it is not trimmed again here. Until the reviewer round (ADJ-D-26-02882, R2.8) this notebook trimmed it a second time, so the submitted Figure 5D used 754–757 CpG sites per comparison instead of 836–837; `11_directionality_trim_check.qmd` documents the difference.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false

# Additional packages (tidyverse, here, janitor, glue loaded via .Rprofile)
pacman::p_load(scales, ggtext, install = FALSE)

conflicted::conflict_prefer_all("dplyr", quiet = TRUE)

source(here("custom_func/display_scientific_notation.R"))
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data

es_long_filtered <- read_rds(here("validation/output/es_long_filtered_AddNeuroMed.rds"))
```

The scatter plots in the main comparison document show that several CpGs have opposing effect directions between AGES and AddNeuroMed. To formally assess whether effect directions are more concordant than expected by chance, we perform binomial sign tests.

## Prepare Directionality Data

```{r}
#| label: prepare-directionality-data

directionality_data <- es_long_filtered |>
  mutate(
    ages_direction = sign(ages_effect_size),
    addneuromed_direction = sign(addneuromed_effect_size),
    concordant = ages_direction == addneuromed_direction &
                 ages_direction != 0 & addneuromed_direction != 0
  ) |>
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_concordant = sum(concordant, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_discordant = n_total - n_concordant,
    prop_concordant = n_concordant / n_total,
    .by = c(addneuromed_comparison, ages_trajectory)
  )
```

## Binomial Sign Test

For each AddNeuroMed comparison and AGES trajectory combination, we test whether the proportion of CpGs with concordant effect directions (both positive or both negative) is significantly greater than 50% (what would be expected by chance).

```{r}
#| label: binomial-sign-test

# Perform binomial sign test for each comparison x trajectory combination
binomial_results <- directionality_data |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    binom_test = list(binom.test(n_concordant, n_total, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater")),
    ci_lower = binom_test$conf.int[1],
    ci_upper = binom_test$conf.int[2],
    binom_pval = binom_test$p.value
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-binom_test) |>
  mutate(
    ages_trajectory = fct_relevel(ages_trajectory, "prev", "mci2incid", "normal2incid", "stable_mci", "normal2mci"),
    significance = case_when(
      binom_pval < 0.001 ~ "***",
      binom_pval < 0.01 ~ "**",
      binom_pval < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

# Display summary table
binomial_results |>
  select(
    addneuromed_comparison, ages_trajectory, n_total, n_concordant, n_discordant,
    prop_concordant, ci_lower, ci_upper, binom_pval, significance
  ) |>
  arrange(addneuromed_comparison, ages_trajectory) |>
  mutate(
    prop_concordant = scales::percent(prop_concordant, accuracy = 0.1),
    ci_95 = glue("{scales::percent(ci_lower, accuracy = 0.1)} - {scales::percent(ci_upper, accuracy = 0.1)}"),
    binom_pval = display_scientific_notation(binom_pval)
  ) |>
  select(-ci_lower, -ci_upper) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "AddNeuroMed Comparison", "AGES Trajectory", "N Total", "N Concordant",
      "N Discordant", "% Concordant", "P-value", "Sig.", "95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Binomial sign test results for effect direction concordance between AGES and AddNeuroMed"
  )
```

## Interpretation

A significant p-value (< 0.05) indicates that the proportion of CpGs with concordant effect directions is significantly greater than 50%, providing evidence that the AGES and AddNeuroMed studies show consistent effect directions beyond what would be expected by chance.

## Directionality Heatmap

```{r}
#| label: fig-directionality-heatmap
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

# Create heatmap of concordance proportions
directionality_plot <- binomial_results |>
  mutate(
    sig_label = glue("{scales::percent(prop_concordant, accuracy = 1)}{significance}")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ages_trajectory, y = addneuromed_comparison, fill = prop_concordant)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_label), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#d73027",
    mid = "#ffffbf",
    high = "#1a9850",
    midpoint = 0.5,
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "prev" = "Prevalent",
    "mci2incid" = "MCI->Incident",
    "normal2incid" = "Normal->Incident",
    "stable_mci" = "Stable MCI",
    "normal2mci" = "Normal->MCI"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "AGES Dementia Trajectory",
    y = "AddNeuroMed Diagnostic Comparison",
    fill = "Proportion\nConcordant",
    title = "Effect Direction Concordance: AGES vs AddNeuroMed",
    subtitle = "Binomial sign test (* p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )

print(directionality_plot)
```

## Directionality Barplot

```{r}
#| label: fig-directionality-barplot
#| fig-cap: "Significance of effect direction concordance between AGES and AddNeuroMed"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

# Filter to requested trajectories and comparisons
barplot_data <- binomial_results |>
  filter(
    ages_trajectory %in% c("normal2incid", "mci2incid", "prev"),
    addneuromed_comparison %in% c("AD vs CN", "MCI vs CN")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    neg_log10_p = -log10(binom_pval),
    ages_trajectory = fct_relevel(ages_trajectory, "normal2incid", "mci2incid", "prev"),
    # Rename comparison for legend
    comparison_label = case_match(
      addneuromed_comparison,
      "AD vs CN" ~ "AD",
      "MCI vs CN" ~ "MCI"
    )
  )

# The "P = 0.05" label starts left of the first (normal2incid, AD) bar and runs over it,
# so its baseline sits just above that bar; the once-trimmed bar (R2.8) reaches
# -log10(P) = 2.33, which the former fixed position (2.3) overlapped.
p_line_label_y <- barplot_data |>
  dplyr::filter(ages_trajectory == "normal2incid", comparison_label == "AD") |>
  pull(neg_log10_p) |>
  max(-log10(0.05), na.rm = TRUE) + 0.3

# Create dodged barplot
directionality_barplot <- barplot_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ages_trajectory, y = neg_log10_p, fill = comparison_label)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = p_line_label_y, vjust = 0,
           label = "italic(P) == 0.05", hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30", parse = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "-log<sub>10</sub>(Binomial Test <i>P</i>-value)",
    fill = "AddNeuroMed"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.15, 0.8),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

directionality_barplot
```

```{r}
#| label: save-barplot
#| echo: false

ggsave(
  here("validation", "output", "fig_directionality_barplot_AddNeuroMed.png"),
  directionality_barplot,
  width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300,
  device = ragg::agg_png
)

write_rds(
  directionality_barplot,
  here("validation", "output", "fig_directionality_barplot_AddNeuroMed.rds")
)

# Sign-test table for all fifteen comparison x trajectory combinations (reviewer R2.8)
write_rds(
  binomial_results,
  here("validation", "output", "directionality_results_AddNeuroMed.rds")
)
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r}
#| label: directionality-summary

# Overall summary across all comparisons
overall_summary <- binomial_results |>
  summarise(
    mean_concordance = mean(prop_concordant),
    min_concordance = min(prop_concordant),
    max_concordance = max(prop_concordant),
    n_significant = sum(binom_pval < 0.05),
    n_total_tests = n(),
    .by = addneuromed_comparison
  )

overall_summary |>
  mutate(
    across(c(mean_concordance, min_concordance, max_concordance), ~scales::percent(., accuracy = 0.1))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "AddNeuroMed Comparison", "Mean Concordance", "Min Concordance",
      "Max Concordance", "N Significant Tests", "N Total Tests"
    ),
    caption = "Summary of effect direction concordance across AGES trajectories"
  )
```
